items.q: A benefit that comes with a cost is a…
Doing a task by machine instead of by hand is…

choices: have no downsides at all for anyone
have no upsides at all for anyone
reduce some accidents but change drivers' jobs
items.why: Every advance has a benefit for someone and a cost for someone else: fewer crashes, perhaps, and changed jobs for drivers.

items.q: Self-checkout: faster lines for shoppers; the career tradeoff is…
choices: fewer cashier jobs, new technician jobs
no change to any job at all
cheaper food and the same jobs
items.why: Automation changes jobs more than it erases them: fewer cashiers are needed, and new technicians keep the machines running.

items.q: A map app that picks your route saves time. A cost is…
choices: you may stop learning your way around
it is always wrong about the time
it needs no battery at all
items.why: If the app always picks the route, you may stop learning your way around. That is a hidden cost of the time it saves.

items.q: When a technology works worse for some groups because of how it was built or tested, that is…
Face unlock works badly for some skin tones. Most likely cause?
choices: phones are too small to see a face
it is a cipher nobody can crack
it was tested with a group that all looked alike
items.why: Bias usually comes from who was missing in testing. A testing group that all looked alike cannot show where face unlock fails.

items.q: A "best lunch" survey skipped every vegetarian. The result is…
choices: fair, because most students eat meat
accurate, because the sample was large
biased, because a group is missing
fine, vegetarians can vote next time
items.why: A whole group was never asked, so the result speaks only for the rest. Missing a group makes data biased, however big the sample.

items.q: Users struggle to read the screen in bright sun. Which recommendation helps them and others?
items.why: High contrast was made for low vision, and everyone uses it in bright sun. Designing for the edges helps everyone.

items.q: Tricking a person into giving away information, like a message pretending to be from the school office, is…
You add a free sound effect from a sound library to your game. Besides giving credit, what should you check first?
choices: its license: what it lets you do
that it is the loudest one
that nobody else has used it
that it is the newest file

items.q: Posting your full name, school and daily route online is risky because…
choices: it uses too much data each month
strangers can use it to trick or find you
it is boring for other people
it is illegal in every country
items.why: Your name, school and route are the facts tricks start with. A stranger can use them to fool you or to find you.

items.q: Making your high scores public: a benefit is competition; a risk is…
choices: it shows who played and when
items.why: Public scores show your name and when you played. That tells strangers more about you than the score itself.

items.q: You use a library's code in your game. The license asks for…
items.why: Reusing code means following its license, and most licenses ask for attribution: credit written the way the license says.
